page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM. Notably, this instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions, and the CPU allocation is shared.

Benchmark data highlights the computational and memory capabilities of this configuration. The system achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 85,426.66 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 96,293.69, which is rated as strong. Memory performance is characterized by a top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 7,649.82 GB/sec, alongside a strong large block write bandwidth of 135.84 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrated top-tier LLM inference speeds with a small 135M model, processing 10,308.98 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 377.14 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of 960 GB of RAM and four enterprise-grade H100 GPUs represents a high-density hardware profile optimized for parallel processing. However, the shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage are key architectural tradeoffs to consider. This server is designed for workloads such as large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, and complex physical simulations that leverage GPU acceleration and massive memory footprints.
